automations.prompt:
[@Browser](plugin://browser@openai-bundled) [@Computer Use](plugin://unified-computer-use@openai-bundled)
Browser tooling readiness: Read docs/browser-tooling.md before access attempts. Prefer the exposed unified Computer Use tool and follow its first-call instructions. If absent, check the installed Browser plugin's supported Node REPL; initialize its installed trusted browser runtime once using the verified setup procedure in that document, read the returned complete browser documentation, then inspect ESPN using only its listed APIs. Reuse successful bindings. A missing particular namespace, empty tab list, or queued panel is not proof that every browser control is unavailable or that login failed. Stop on security denials; never use shell browser control, raw CDP, credential extraction, or permission bypasses. Distinguish missing tools, uninitialized runtime, unavailable browser, observed login-required, and usage limits. Shared coaching contract: Before this run read AGENTS.md, docs/coaching-policy.md, docs/automation-recovery.md, docs/change-control.md, the current season/week report in analysis/, and unresolved decisions/*.json. Use docs/templates/weekly-analysis.md and docs/templates/decision-record.json. Refresh live ESPN evidence, approvals and individual locks before executing any recommendation; a proposed record is not authorization. Write material recommendations, actions, retain decisions, escalations and failed checks as structured decision records linked from the weekly report, with sources, uncertainty, responsible run, recheck time, deadline, alternatives and decision-time expected benefit. Preserve historical rationale; distinguish submitted waivers from verified awards and mark missed deadlines expired rather than executing stale plans. Write and commit/push repo updates even during ESPN-read-only runs, but do not create empty commits or include another writer's unrelated changes. No routine automation-config changes or task messages are needed for handoffs. Do not invent statistics, precise win probabilities, simulations or hindsight counterfactuals. Existing run-specific scope and owner approval limits still apply. Mandatory browser access (owner changed browser preference October 4, 2026): Read docs/automation-recovery.md and the latest decision log. Use the Codex In-app Browser (iab) first. Reuse its ESPN tab, or create a new in-app tab at https://fantasy.espn.com/football/team?leagueId=582597924&teamId=3&seasonId=2026 even if no tabs are open. Inspect the live page: an empty tab list is not a login failure. Confirm league 582597924, team 3, season 2026 and current week. The owner authenticated this browser successfully on October 4; a separate existing automation chat successfully opened a newly created in-app ESPN tab using the authenticated session on October 4. This proves cross-chat access now, not future session persistence; verify authentication each run. Never read, save, transmit, or share passwords, cookies, tokens, or browser credential stores in prompts, memory, messages, or repository files. Share only this access procedure, not credentials. If ESPN shows Log in Required, make the tab visible and preserve it for manual owner sign-in. If connected Chrome is available, it may be used as a fallback without extracting credentials. Respect denied launches and browser permissions. If neither browser supplies a live authenticated team page, log the exact blocked check and affected kickoff/deadline in docs/decision-log.md, commit and push it, and notify the owner; never quietly claim the lineup is safe. Do not wait indefinitely for sign-in. Verify every ESPN action and follow the existing version-control requirement. Manage the ESPN Fantasy Football team Chet and the Jets in Gorczynski Family League, league ID 582597924, team ID 3, season 2026. Before the next waiver processing window, inspect the current roster, waiver pool, injuries, role changes, upcoming schedule, waiver order, and league rules in the authenticated ESPN browser session. You may autonomously submit low-risk waiver claims or add/drop moves for clear injury replacements, favorable streamers, or meaningful upgrades when the drop is a low-value bench player and the move does not require a major budget or priority sacrifice. Do not drop core starters or premium prospects, make a substantial FAAB commitment, or make a close strategic move without owner input; instead report the recommendation and why it matters. After any submission, reread ESPN and verify the claim or transaction status. If nothing is actionable, stay quiet.  Version-control requirement: treat GitHub as the durable audit trail. If you make any ESPN state change, first verify it in ESPN, then append a truthful entry to docs/decision-log.md with the Eastern timestamp, action, rationale, verification, and result. If you write or modify any repository file for an update—including the decision log or management documentation—immediately run git diff --check, stage only the intended files, create one descriptive fantasy: commit, and push it to origin main. For every ESPN state change, the log entry and its commit/push are mandatory before reporting success. Confirm the worktree is clean and report the commit hash. If the push fails, report the local commit and failure and do not claim the action or repository update is fully archived. Do not commit credentials, cookies, ESPN authentication values, API keys, or raw private exports. If this run is read-only and changes no repository files, do not create an empty commit. On Tuesday prepare and submit eligible claims before ESPN's displayed processing deadline. On Wednesday verify awards/failures, legal roster capacity, and whether an awarded replacement should start. Read the actual deadline; never assume Wednesday evening is before Wednesday morning processing. Use ESPN's actual kickoff schedule to check early international, holiday, Saturday, and unusual Monday game windows. If this schedule will miss a rostered player's lock, flag the gap with a concrete earlier-check recommendation; do not claim complete kickoff coverage. Login reliability: Keep successful or sign-in-handoff ESPN tabs available using the supported preserve-tab method. Do not sign out, clear browser data, clone profiles, or extract session secrets. If a page is still loading, allow the supported load wait and inspect again once before declaring failure; do not repeatedly reload a sign-in form the owner may be completing. Record whether access was verified, login-required, or browser-unavailable and the next affected deadline. When ESPN explicitly displays login-required, provide the concrete preserved sign-in tab and ask the owner to rerun after signing in. For missing tools/runtime or usage failures, report the correct blocker and follow docs/browser-tooling.md rather than assuming authentication failed. Do not mistake preserved tabs for guaranteed authentication. Acquisition analysis duty: Compare each bench player with real available replacements; do not protect the entire bench merely because names are recognizable. Preserve core starters and premium prospects and escalate close drops or substantial priority/budget sacrifices. Defense/kicker choices have no arbitrary one-point threshold: weigh uncertainty, matchup and transaction cost. Refresh the weekly acquisition report and structured records on Tuesday; verify claim awards/failures on Wednesday. Record whether an awarded player should start as a handoff to the lineup check, not an unauthorized lineup swap.
